26 A pipe of length 100 cm is open at both ends. A loudspeaker situated at one end of the pipe can
emit sound of different wavelengths.
100 cm
loudspeaker
pipe
At which wavelength can a stationary wave be produced in the pipe?
A
50 cm
B
75 cm
C
150 cm
D
300 cm

hints: Notice the pipe is $100\text{ cm}$ long and open at both ends, so there must be a displacement antinode at the loudspeaker end and at the far end.
Recall the open-open resonance rule that the length must contain a whole number of half-wavelengths: $L = n\lambda/2$ with $n = 1, 2, 3...$.
Test each listed wavelength in $\text{cm}$ by finding $\lambda/2$ and checking which one divides $100\text{ cm}$ exactly.
walkthrough: Identify the given length $L = 100\text{ cm}$ and the boundary condition: an open end is a displacement antinode for sound, so both ends must be antinodes.
State the stationary wave condition for a pipe open at both ends: $L = n\lambda/2$, where $n$ is an integer number of half-wavelength segments.
Rearrange for allowed wavelengths: $\lambda = 2L/n = 200/n\text{ cm}$ with $n = 1, 2, 3...$.
Check the options: for $50\text{ cm}$, $\lambda/2 = 25\text{ cm}$ and $100/25 = 4$, an integer; for $75\text{ cm}$, $150\text{ cm}$ and $300\text{ cm}$ the value $2L/\lambda$ is not an integer.
Therefore only $50\text{ cm}$ fits an exact number of half-wavelengths with antinodes at both ends. This is option A.

A.explanation: With $L = 100\text{ cm}$ and $\lambda = 50\text{ cm}$, $L = 2 \times \lambda/2$, so two half-wavelengths fit with antinodes at both open ends.

B.explanation: $75\text{ cm}$ does not satisfy $L = n\lambda/2$ because $100/37.5$ is not an integer number of half-wavelengths.

C.explanation: $150\text{ cm}$ gives $\lambda/2 = 75\text{ cm}$, which does not divide $100\text{ cm}$ into a whole number of half-wavelengths.

D.explanation: $300\text{ cm}$ is longer than the $100\text{ cm}$ pipe and its half-wavelength of $150\text{ cm}$ cannot fit between two open-end antinodes.
